steps.text: Combine evaporated milk, milk, sugar, cornstarch, and egg in a saucepan over medium heat. Cook and stir until thick. Remove pudding from heat; add vanilla and mix well.
Arrange a layer of wafers in a large bowl or casserole dish. Pour pudding over wafers and top with banana slices. Refrigerate until chilled, about 1 hour.

raw_recipe.headline: Kentucky Banana Pudding
raw_recipe.description: This banana pudding is made with evaporated milk and features a crust of vanilla wafers topped with creamy pudding and a layer of sliced bananas.
raw_recipe.name: Kentucky Banana Pudding

review.reviewBody: This recipe is really good. I only had sweetened condensed milk so I used that instead of evaporated so it was a little too sweet for me but not for anyone else. I had to make a lot of it, so I also mixed in a pack of instant pudding. Hint: Add a tablespoon of lemon juice to pudding and your bananas won't turn brown.

I have made this several times. I use a 9x13 pan. I double the pudding recipe, use 7 bananas, use 1 1/4 pkgs of nila wafers. I also put enough lemon juice on the bananas to make sure they don't discolor. For the whipped topping, i use heavy whipping cream. I use 16 oz, 1/2 tsp tartar(helps stabilize the topping), 1/4-1/2 cup powdered sugar and 1tsp of vanilla extract. Make sure to heat the mixture and dissolve the sugar in the milk(i just used whole milk not evaporated) before adding the egg. I Reserve 1/2 cup of milk to mix with the cornstarch. Then i add the egg when the mixture is warm. Don't let the mixture to hot before adding the egg or y'all get scrambled eggs. Then, i add the cornstarch/milk mixture to the rest. Whisking vigorously until it becomes thick. I usually make the pudding a day before that way it's not hot when prepping it. It was such a great recipe.

Good recipe with my changes include: Use two egg yolks not one egg Cook custard stirring constantly until thickened. This requires time and patience. Alternate cookie/ custard/sliced banana slices. Finish with a meringue topping using the two leftover egg whites. Cover pudding completely to edges of dish. Broil until meringue is just very lightly browned. Cool to room temperature then refrigerate. Note: use your favorite recipe/method for meringue.

First, I doubled the recipe like some reviewers suggested, and it turned out being the perfect amount for my Pyrex triffle dish. Secondly, I decreased the sugar to 3/4 cup like some of the reviewers suggested. Next, I used only 2% milk because I didn't want an aftertaste like some of the reviewers commented and I also wanted to make this pudding 100% from scratch. Note: Dissolve the cornstarch in 1/2 cup of milk first and stir the lumps out. Pour the milk in the saucepan first, then the sugar, and after it dissolves, the egg (before the pan heats too much and creates scrambled eggs), and the cornstarch mixture. I used a stainless steel pot and a whisk. Patience is key because if you take it off of the heat too early, the custard will never thicken. I whisked for a long time and kept pulling the whisk up out of the pan to see if it had cooked; and eventually, there was no more egg white globs, everything was all dissolved and had a common consistency. 

Following the advice of one of the reviewers, I added the bananas to the hot custard after it thickened. I thought that I could skip the step of slicing and placing the bananas on the cookies, which can be time consuming. But by trying to shortcut, it left the bananas tasting "raw" with a bite. The cookies had softened, but the bananas were now crunchy. How gross. But adding the bananas to the hot custard flavored it so much that the actual bananas weren't necessary. The consistency of the custard was nice.

We loved this! Following some other reviews, I made these changes: 3 cups whole milk, 2 egg yolks, 1/2 cup sugar & 1 tsp vanilla. I did not use evaporated milk. I used the egg whites plus one more to make meringue. I layered it with the bananas in the middle. After putting on the meringue I put it under the broiler for a few minutes to brown. It turned out great!

As others suggest it is to sweet. I will cut back the sugar to 3/4 cup next time. It had a very good flavor otherwise and was easy to make. I also arrange my bananas under my pudding so they do not brown. Putting them on top is just asking for all kinds of ugliness.

I added 1 5.9 ounce box of instant banana cream pudding mix and 1/2 cup of organic unsweetened nondairy almond beverage. I also ground up the vanilla wafers and added some butter to make a crust for the bottom layer.
Great recipe! I only used 3/4 cup of sugar, replaced regular milk with coconut milk, and added a layer of bananas on top of the cookie crust. Absolutely delicious!

We've made it like this for years. The only changes I made were all whole milk, plus a dash of salt (1 tsp for a triple batch). I tempered the eggs to avoid curdling (by that I mean I beat the eggs seperately, then cooked the remaining mixture until hot, then spooned the hot mixture about 3 cups but a cup at a time into the eggs, stirring constantly. Then added the egg mixture to the remaining pudding to keep cooking.) Stirring constantly also prevents sticking. Great! Thanks for posting.

I made this for Father’s Day. Only made a couple changes per other reviewers. I did not have any Nilla Wafers but I had a ready made graham cracker pie shell. The bananas I covered in lemon juice then placed them on the bottom of the pie shell. I added a dash of cinnamon and nutmeg. Also dissolved the corn starch in part of the milk. When it cooled I tcrea. Worked perfectly! The next day I realized I forgot to ask my husband if he liked it and looked in the fridge - OVER HALF WAS GONE. I guess he liked it! Thank you very much for such a great recipe!

I feel bad for the folks who said their pudding never thickened, and I think the recipe should really stress that you don't stop cooking until the mixture is pudding thick. On my electric stove, I had to cook the pudding for quite a bit longer than 10 minutes to get that thick consistency. I even brought a stool over to the stove because you have to stir that pudding constantly, especially as it gets really hot. At the end I added some vanilla and a tablespoon of butter to up the flavor. Delicious.
A perfect recipe as is, tastes just like my grandma’s. A keeper!! Thank you!!

My dad loved butterscotch pudding, every holiday it was a staple on the dessert table. With the addition of one tablespoon butterscotch flavoring, this would be a good way to make instead of using a boxed pudding.

This recipe was better than I thought it would be. It had a good taste and relatively simple to make. And importantly, a better taste than using a pudding mix. I mistakenly bought graham crackers instead of the vanilla wafers and ended up laying the bottom with graham crackers. It still turned out good. Next time I will use both. I recommend this recipe.
Easily to make and has a good flavor.

This is like the banana pudding I grew up on except we start with the cookie layer and then alternate sliced bananas and cookies in layers with the pudding and end with a layer if bananas and cookies on top and then whipped cream if you like. 🥰
Second time this week. Taste like my grandmothers. Keeper
My wife loves this Banana Pudding. I used Chessman cookies this time just for her.
Did not set up and banana turned brown
Definitely making this again!!!
